classification.difficultyReason: Calculate volumes from two diameter-height pairs and justify which cylinder is larger.

content.prompt: Determine which of these cylinders has the largest volume.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, upright cylinder A at left
spec.description: Upright cylinder with grey top, central A label, solid full top ellipse, solid front bottom arc and dashed rear bottom arc.
spec.mathematics: Diameter 7.7 and axial height 15; no physical length unit is supplied. Bottom double-headed horizontal dimension denotes diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Given dimensions and A identifier only.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, horizontal cylinder B to the right of A
spec.description: Horizontal cylinder with full visible grey left ellipse, central B label, solid top and bottom generators, solid far outer arc and dashed far inner arc.
spec.mathematics: Diameter 12 and axial length 8.2; no physical length unit is supplied. Vertical double-headed dimension denotes diameter.
spec.answerVisibility: Given dimensions and B identifier only.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}r_A&=7.7\div2=3.85\\V_A&=\pi r_A^2h_A\\V_A&=\pi\times3.85^2\times15\\V_A&=222.3375\pi\\V_A&\approx698.5\\r_B&=12\div2=6\\V_B&=\pi r_B^2h_B\\V_B&=\pi\times6^2\times8.2\\V_B&=295.2\pi\\V_B&\approx927.4\end{align*}$
Volumes are in cubic units. Since $295.2\pi>222.3375\pi$, cylinder B is larger.
